thread:
alice: Quick heads-up — onboarding run for `sienna-embed-small` (int8 quant) shows a ~6% drop in recall@10 vs fp16 on our prod-recall-bench. numbers below. anyone seen this pattern before? :thinking:

ben: ugh. can you paste the exact metrics and the eval command you used?

alice: sure, short dump:
```
Model: sienna-embed-small
Precision: int8 (PTQ)
Dataset: prod-recall-bench (100k queries, 1M corpus)
Metric: recall@10
fp16 baseline: 0.842
int8 run: 0.781
run_id: r-2026-03-18-09
```
Command: `python eval/recall.py --model sienna-embed-small --weights ./runs/r-2026-03-18-09/weights.pt --norm cosine --dataset prod-recall-bench --topk 10`

carla: first guesses: (1) quantization artefacts (PTQ bad) (2) mismatch in normalization (l2 vs cosine) at index time (3) accidental shift in tokenizer vocab or preprocessing. did you reindex the DB after quantizing?

alice: i re-ran indexing with the int8 weights, yes. `index_version: v3-int8`. indexes were built on the same commit. also used `--norm cosine` both for query and corpus.

ben: can you sanity-check embedding norms distribution? if quant lowers dynamic range, cosine might flip ordering. quick script: `python tools/emb_stats.py --index ./indexes/v3-int8` should show mean/std and any clipping.

alice: ran that, outputs: mean_norm=0.98, std_norm=0.12 for fp16; mean_norm=0.43, std_norm=0.05 for int8. so magnitude collapsed. looks like post-quant scaling mismatch.

dave: that points to missing scale/rescale step in our int8 export path. when we do PTQ we need to apply the per-channel scales to the accumulator at inference. maybe the runtime is using fused kernels but missing the dequant multiply? any logs from the serving shim?

alice: checked runtime logs, nothing obvious. but eval-bench used local inference harness, not the full runtime. harness command: `tools/run_local_infer.sh --weights ./runs/... --quant int8 --backend torchscript`

carla: try running a tiny sample with both fp16 and int8 and compare pairwise cosine distances and nearest neighbors for a few queries. if neighbors reorder massively then it's quant issue. also check that we used `normalize=True` in the embedding head both at train/export time and during eval.

alice: did pairwise check for sample qid=8312:
```
fp16 top3: [doc_125, doc_512, doc_77]
int8 top3: [doc_512, doc_125, doc_77]
cosine diffs: fp16->int8: [0.78, 0.76, 0.75] vs int8: [0.51, 0.50, 0.49]
```
ordering slightly changed and magnitudes much lower.

ben: ok that confirms collapse. next steps: (A) re-run quant with per-channel calibration and per-tensor fallback for embedding head; (B) try FP16->QAT quick fine-tune (one epoch) to see if recover; (C) test cosine after re-applying normalization as a post-processing step (i.e., renormalize embeddings after quantize/infer). assign?

alice: i'll take (C) and (A) quick re-run today. i'll open a PR with re-export scripts.

carla: i'll spin up a QAT experiment on a small shard (B) — would like to know if model capacity helps.

dave: i'll add a runtime check in the torchscript loader to assert scale presence and warn if mean_norm < 0.6 for a sanity threshold. will open a tiny patch.

eval-bot: automated note: baseline fp16 recall@10=0.842 (run r-2026-03-10-21), latest int8 job r-2026-03-18-09 recall@10=0.781. Alert severity: medium. See /ci/evals/r-2026-03-18-09 for logs. :robot_face:

alice: thanks — i'll post updates here after the PTQ with per-channel scales finishes (should be ~2h). tagging @dave for runtime patch review when ready. :thumbsup:
